numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Year is truncated to 32 bits for second-resolution dates beyond year 2**31: DatetimeIndex.year / Series.dt.year wrote the year into an int32 array so it came back wrapped; is_leap_year took its leap status from the wrapped year; day_of_year and ISO week were wrong on the scalar path; the isocalendar year column was unsigned so years before year 1 wrapped (year -100 came out as 4294967196). Also DatetimeIndex + pd.DateOffset(months=1) on the max int64 second-resolution index returned a wrapped date '219250469-01-04 15:30:07'.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Year accessors should raise instead of returning a wrapped year; negative years should be representable in the isocalendar year column (now Int32); an ISO year beyond the int32 range raises. Scalar day_of_year and ISO week should be computed from the correct year.

isocalendar() on dates before year 1 (unsigned year column wrapping)
DatetimeIndex with M8[s] dtype at int64 max, plus pd.DateOffset(months=1)
scalar day_of_year / ISO week computation on out-of-int32-range years

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: years beyond the int32 range (year 2**31 and above); negative years before year 1 for isocalendar; example year -100 wrapped to 4294967196; year 3010362559 example from period.pyx
category_specific_evidence: Commit: DatetimeIndex.year and Series.dt.year wrote the year into an int32 array so a second-resolution date beyond year 2**31 came back wrapped; they now raise instead.

Commit: is_leap_year took its leap status from the wrapped year; ccalendar get_day_of_year, get_week_of_year and get_iso_calendar took the year as a C int, so day_of_year and ISO week were wrong on the scalar path too.
PR body: isocalendar() year column was unsigned, so years before year 1 wrapped: year -100 came out as 4294967196; now Int32, and an ISO year beyond int32 range raises.
PR body: y_of_year returned 363 rather than 364; scalar vs vectorized comparison cannot detect this because both sides truncated identically.

Issue#66549 reproducer: pd.date_range('2000-01-03', periods=1, unit='s') + pd.offsets.SemiMonthEnd(2**32) gives '2000-01-15', equal to SemiMonthEnd(0); QuarterEnd(2**32) gives '2000-03-31', equal to QuarterEnd(0). Offsets with count 2**32 wrap to zero effect.

Issue#66549 reproducer: pd.Timestamp.min + pd.Timedelta(-1,'ns') gives NaT; DatetimeIndex([Timestamp.min]) + Timedelta(-1,'ns') gives NaT in datetime64[ns]; TimedeltaIndex([Timedelta.min]) - Timedelta(1,'ns') gives NaT; PeriodIndex([Period(ordinal=-2**63+1, freq='D')]) - 1 gives NaT.
PR body: period.pyx cdef int pyear() truncates similarly: Period(ordinal=2**40, freq='D').year gives -1284604737 for year 3010362559 (not addressed in PR).
Test diff: test_isocalendar expected frame year column changed from UInt32 to Int32 via astype, with week and day remaining UInt32.
reproduction_risks: Correctness property violated is a silent wrap-around of year values through 32-bit truncation; expected values must be computed independently (not via the same truncated scalar/vector path) to detect the bug.
Behavior after fix is raising rather than returning wrapped values for years beyond int32; a reproduction must expect an exception for out-of-range ISO years.
Period.year and Timestamp.isocalendar() have separate, unfixed truncation or OverflowError behavior above year 9999 and should not be conflated with the fixed path.
Offset and NaT reproducers in the issue are separate overflow cases from the year truncation and may not be the same root cause.
